patterns: Product-trust announcement wins the day: @sama's 'We're now testing Private Inference… Stronger privacy protections will make frontier AI useful for a lot more work' hit 1.17M views in under a day. Name the new capability, then say in one line why it unlocks more real work

Build-log with hard numbers: @karpathy's 'Opus 5.5… 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)' hit 974K views with 8.2K bookmarks (more than half its 15K likes). Time + volume + a deadpan 'it works' + a bullet list of sources is highly saveable
One new word, one line: @sama's 'I don't think I'd heard the word "hyperstitioning" before, but it's a good one' reached 927K. Curating a single sticky term travels further than explaining it
Emoji-only momentum claim: @OfficialLoganK's 'Neon usage is 📈📈📈' hit 420K views and 8.7K likes from four words. Works only when the audience already knows the product
Inversion of a famous line: @garrytan's Bostrom clip ('if anyone builds it everyone dies' → 'if nobody builds it everyone dies') reached 396K. Flip a phrase people already know

Two-line identity punch: @AlexHormozi's 'success in life comes down to being able to say "I'm not for everyone." And meaning it.' hit 99K with 5K likes. Short claim, then a three-word second line that raises the stakes

drafts.angle: Privacy as the unlock, applied to pre-launch creative (rides @sama 'Private Inference', 1.17M, new today)
drafts.draft_en:
Privacy is turning into a feature frontier AI has to ship.

For marketing teams this is obvious.

Unreleased campaigns are some of the most sensitive files a brand has. Launch dates, pricing, claims legal hasn't cleared yet.

If you're using AI to check creative before it goes live, ask where that creative ends up.

Pre-launch review should be private by default.
drafts.video_tip: 30s talking head, phone vertical. Open on a screenshot of Sam's post, then cut to a blurred 'UNRELEASED' ad mockup with a padlock overlay while you read lines 3-4. Close on the last line as a text card. Burned-in captions, native upload, credit @sama in the first reply.

drafts.angle: Build-log numbers → the verification gap (rides @karpathy '7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works', 974K, 8.2K bookmarks, new today)
drafts.draft_en:
An agent wrote 45K lines of code in 7 hours.

The same thing is happening in marketing.

An agent can make 500 ad variants overnight. Every one still has to clear:

• brand rules
• legal claims
• platform policy

"It works" and "it's approved" are different things.

The teams that win will check at the speed they generate.
drafts.video_tip: 40s screen recording: a counter ticking up to 500 generated ad variants, then each one passes through three gates labeled brand / legal / platform with approve-fix-block stamps. Voiceover reads the bullets. End on the last line. Vertical, captions on, link in the first reply only.

drafts.angle: Two-line identity punch, applied to brand safety (rides @AlexHormozi 'I'm not for everyone. And meaning it.', 99K, 5K likes, new today)
drafts.draft_en:
A lot of good marketing comes down to being able to say "this ad doesn't ship."

And meaning it.
drafts.video_tip: 10-15s, single shot: you at a desk say line 1 to camera, pause, say 'And meaning it.' Hard cut to black with a BLOCK stamp. No music, captions burned in, native upload. Use a quiet thumbnail with the first line as text.
